::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Please how solve this Improper Integral](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2195112/please-how-solve-this-improper-integral), asked by [Trucker](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/153069/trucker) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2017-03-20; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Please how solve this Improper Integral ... $$\int_{1}^{+\infty}\frac{1}{\sqrt[x]{e}}dx$$... i know how to solve $$\int_1^{+\infty} \sqrt[x]{e}$$ I create a Taylor Polynomial and integrate, but this is a little hard. 
> if it is possible...
:::

Presumably you were able to show that $\int_1^\infty \sqrt[x]{e}\,dx$ diverges, because
$$\lim_{x\to\infty} \sqrt[x]{e} = 1$$
But it follows from the above that
$$\lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{1}{\sqrt[x]{e}} = \frac{1}{1} = 1$$
so $\int_1^\infty \frac{1}{\sqrt[x]{e}}\,dx$ diverges, too.
